blocks.body:
# Saudi lead research: revised pre-build buyer plan

Research review dated 5 September 2026. Three parallel reviews covered the list, qualification logic and discovery sources. The canonical list and application remain unchanged.

## Executive Summary

Recommend excluding 38 prospects, investigating five first, and retaining seven other holds. None currently has sufficient evidence to confirm all revised gates. This is a review of all stored records and 156 evidence summaries, supplemented by selected live checks; it is not 50 new external profile verifications.

The desired buyer has a specific first software project whose core functionality remains unbuilt and a supported maximum of two software builders. Paid external-delivery demand is a separate commercial question.

## Why the current list overstates fit

Forty-seven records explicitly mark outsourcing likelihood unknown, yet 44 are labeled qualified and all 50 have high qualification confidence. At least 26 are labeled launched or operating; further built products appear among unknown-stage rows. All seven A labels lack the qualitative support required by the stored rubric.

The team-ceiling gap is universal. This does not mean all teams are large; it means the evidence cannot yet establish that they are small enough. The total-employee field is also missing frequently, but total employees and software builders are different quantities.

## Apply gates before commercial scoring

Require supported identity and authority, a specific Saudi-market build, unbuilt core functionality, no more than two current software builders, and a current initiative. An unresolved gate stays on hold; a failed gate makes the project out of scope. A company-controlled full-team statement can support a maximum; a partial LinkedIn roster only establishes a visible minimum.

Count hands-on technical founders, employees and known contractors. Record assigned vendors separately. A functional private app can already fail the product gate; a brochure site does not disqualify an SME’s first custom build. Avoid industry-wide exclusions.

For confirmed fits, score build commitment (6), paid external intent (6), available project funds (4) and timing (4). Unknowns earn no affirmative points. Equity-only hiring and noncash credits do not prove a paid development opportunity. Preserve those candidates in a research pool when otherwise relevant.

## Recheck the best unresolved candidates first

urCASH, Wathba, Jadi and Vision Mate have useful pre-build signals, with current team and commercial gaps. BookMyGuide is lower priority because its Saudi entry and current activity remain unresolved. The seven other holds are Smart Quotation, Gaia, Ballora, Zakn AI, GreenVision, Suhail and Mara.

STOQA’s [available Android product](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=ai.stoqa.app) supports exclusion for this campaign. [Vision Mate](https://sa.linkedin.com/jobs/view/technical-co-founder-at-vision-mate-4460498663) is an equity-based wearable/AI co-founder opportunity. [Jadi](https://sa.linkedin.com/jobs/view/4399318887) is a closed equity CTO listing. [BookMyGuide’s post](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hayath-kargal-b0b17057_vision2030-ntdp-mvplab-activity-7412319001252618240-2TT5) describes planned Saudi entry and a program application, not a confirmed grant. None is a verified paid-agency lead.

## Find founders earlier and test manual-business demand

Prioritize current pre-incubation admissions, specific public first-build requests, and owners of non-software SMEs planning their first custom product. Use portfolios, funding news and demo days to verify maturity and funds.

[Misk Launchpad](https://hub.misk.org.sa/en/programs/entrepreneurship/misk-launchpad/) lists its next cohort starting 6 September 2026, initially in Ideate. [Sanabil Accelerator](https://mena.500.co/founders/mena/seed-accelerator) requires an MVP and early traction. [StartSmart’s tenth edition](https://startsmartsaudi.com/programs/competitions?page=1) excludes idea-only applicants and offers technical benefits rather than cash. Record exact program, edition and phase. Admission alone proves neither an unbuilt product nor a paid build budget.

Pilot [Antler Riyadh residency](https://www.antler.co/location/menap) introductions and public Saudi first-app briefs. These are discovery experiments; no new yield has been measured. Ordinary LinkedIn remains useful for small exact-name checks. No outreach, interactions or contact enrichment are part of the plan.

## Next steps and success measures

1. Preserve v1 and implement claim-backed v2 eligibility without overwriting research notes. Fix hardcoded verified gates, stage substring inference, automatic review timestamps and unrelated fallback evidence.
2. Calibrate ten contrasting examples, then run independent discovery streams for pre-incubation, public build requests and manual SMEs. Apply the product screen before spending time on deep team enrichment.
3. Verify plausible candidates’ remaining gaps in parallel and publish valid partial batches. Fifty is a goal, not a requirement for data validity.
4. Track unique reviewed candidates, confirmed fits, paid external demand, exclusions and research minutes. Separate discovery attribution from corroboration and preserve v1 yields. After two 20-candidate source passes each yield fewer than two new confirmed fits, pause and redirect that channel.
5. Show product status, supported team ceiling, evidence coverage, paid intent and next research action. Keep evidence grouped by claim in the centered modal.

Acceptance should mean zero unsupported active qualifications. It should not depend on filling exactly 50 rows.

## Caveats and further questions

The 38 exclusions are proposed from recorded evidence, not assertions that every person has been freshly investigated. “Zero confirmed fits” measures evidence sufficiency and does not prove zero suitable founders exist. Public research may leave team ceilings unresolved; do not contact founders to fill those gaps within this scope. The new scoring thresholds are uncalibrated operational rules.

Nine official/program-source checks were attempted; some pages were partial, historical or unreadable. Current website checks did not yield readable urCASH or MVP Lab text. Missing content proves nothing about product or funding. Twelve candidates remain investigable, and no replacement lead count or future source yield is claimed.

Pilot questions: which channel produces confirmed fits fastest, how often do fits want paid external help, whether manual SMEs show more cash readiness, and which programs assign their own providers?

## Full proposed lead and resource revisions

The tables preserve original identities and attach proposed reasons and next checks. Original scores are retained in the companion CSV/JSON for comparison, not endorsed as current v2 priorities.

queue.name: Bashayr Alabbad
queue.product_reason: Founder/job evidence explicitly says the technical co-founder must build the student platform from the ground up.
queue.team_reason: A missing technical co-founder is a strong historical gap signal, not proof of current <=2 software capacity.
queue.next_check: The role is closed and roughly four months old: verify present product and team, then check cash capacity because the offer is negotiable equity.

queue.name: Talal Alharbi
queue.product_reason: Official-site evidence describes a waitlist rather than a public launch, contradicting the stored launched lifecycle label.
queue.team_reason: Founder says three co-founders and no employees. Their hands-on engineering roles and any contractors are unknown; zero employees is not zero developers.
queue.next_check: Check current website/app-store state, audit all three co-founders and contributors, and establish funding or paid build capacity.

queue.name: Abdulrahman Almuqati CIPD
queue.product_reason: The recent role describes a pre-company concept requiring an AI wearable and mobile/cloud implementation.
queue.team_reason: A solo founder and company size of one are recorded, but a complete current roster including contractors and the founder's hands-on capacity is absent.
queue.next_check: Confirm role remains open and no prototype is operational; audit delivery roster; look for cash/grant allocation because the offer is equity-based.

queue.name: Mashhoor Aldubayan
queue.product_reason: The original role explicitly asks one primary founding engineer to produce the first production MVP; this contradicts the stored launched label. The community website is not proof this intended product is launched.
queue.team_reason: The role suggests a delivery gap, but an approved architecture implies earlier technical contribution and hiring may since have completed.
queue.next_check: Check original role closure and whether engineer was hired, confirm first MVP still unbuilt, audit current contributors and cash budget.

queue.name: Hayath Kargal
queue.product_reason: Founder-authored evidence says pre-MVP and planning Saudi pilots, contradicting beta. The coordinator's live recheck shows the post is approximately eight months old, so current product state remains unknown.
queue.team_reason: Two founders are mentioned but software roles and outside contributors are unknown.
queue.next_check: First establish current Saudi presence/operations and whether the pre-MVP project remains active. Then audit product, both founders' technical roles and contributors. MVP Lab was an application, not an award or verified funding.

queue.name: Marya Fawaz
queue.product_reason: Ballora is documented as a graduation project and conference platform; no source establishes the current software lifecycle or a commercial build decision.
queue.team_reason: Fawaz has front-end/design experience, but the full student/project engineering team is unknown.
queue.next_check: Confirm active company/project ownership and authority (official roster names Ghadah Alshehri), current product state, all contributors and a funding path.

queue.name: Badr Al-Malluh
queue.product_reason: Private early access may already contain functioning enterprise software; the stored evidence does not establish an unbuilt core platform.
queue.team_reason: One co-founder/CPTO (Mohammad Rababah) is identified. An 11–50 total band does not prove three engineers or a <=2 upper bound.
queue.next_check: Low-priority check of actual product operation and current engineering roster; do not infer sufficient team from CPTO plus company-size band alone.

queue.name: Yara Alalawi
queue.product_reason: A cloud-dashboard prototype is explicitly described. That can be eligible, but it must be distinguished from already-operating deployed software.
queue.team_reason: Yara explicitly identifies herself as lead engineer/backend architect, establishing at least one builder; other team members and contractors are uncounted.
queue.next_check: Confirm prototype-only state, current team with <=2 upper bound, commercial owner intent and available project funds.

queue.name: Omar Alsumih
queue.product_reason: A first app version was demonstrated and sandbox testing is recorded. This proves some build work, but does not establish public/production operation or whether it remains a prototype.
queue.team_reason: Four total employees and a software-development company category do not prove four software builders or sufficient capacity.
queue.next_check: Low-priority check whether app is operational or just a demo; then current technical-role count. Record the unpaid role/resource constraint as a budget issue.

queue.name: Radhi Alshammari
queue.product_reason: The founder already describes an MVP and supplier onboarding. A company 'building' post does not establish whether the MVP is a mock-up, private pilot or operational product.
queue.team_reason: Internal leadership is mentioned but no role census exists.
queue.next_check: First establish whether the MVP is functional/in use, then audit every current founder and engineer and identify a paid build need.

queue.product_reason: The project advanced to an MVP-building program phase; participation does not tell us whether the MVP was subsequently completed or deployed.
queue.team_reason: Three co-founders are named and technical founders are mentioned, but individual active software roles are not enumerated; do not treat all three as developers automatically.
queue.next_check: Check post-program product progress and the engineering roles of Shatha, Ghadah and Nada; then commercial ownership and funds.

resources.harvest: Run small read-only recent-post searches for exact phrases such as looking for an app development company, MVP development partner, developing our first app, seeking a technical cofounder, أبحث عن شركة برمجة, تطوير تطبيق لمشروعي, نبحث عن شريك تقني, and نعمل على نموذج أولي, then apply Saudi geography terms. Tag paid vendor request, employee vacancy, equity-only co-founder request, or unclear separately; exact-name verification follows discovery.
resources.caveat: These are proposed search phrases, not verified buyer posts. Cofounder or employee searches establish a possible capacity gap but not paid-vendor demand; public post visibility and commercial limits may constrain coverage.

resources.caveat: Program site and its LinkedIn account are one underlying organization, not independent corroboration.
